Much of the telecom stack still runs protocols designed when every participant was a known, trusted operator. SS7 assumes that the node sending a request has a legitimate reason to send it. BGP assumes a network announcing a route actually owns it. Attackers who understand those assumptions can operate inside a carrier for years without triggering a single alert. For telecom CISOs and SOC teams, defending this environment starts with understanding how these attacks actually work.
